# netbox_virtual_circuit (Resource)

From the [official documentation](https://docs.netbox.dev/en/stable/models/circuits/virtualcircuit/):

> A virtual circuit is a logical connection between interfaces that rides on a provider network, for example an L2 service.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbox_virtual_circuit" "example" {
  cid                 = "example"
  provider_network_id = netbox_circuit_provider_network.example.id
  type_id             = netbox_virtual_circuit_type.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cid` (String) Unique circuit ID.
- `provider_network_id` (Number) The ID of the provider network associated with the virtual circuit.
- `type_id` (Number) The ID of the type associated with the virtual circuit.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Free-form comments about the virtual circuit.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values of the object, as a map of field name to value.
- `description` (String) A description of the virtual circuit.
- `owner_id` (Number) The ID of the owner associated with the virtual circuit. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `provider_account_id` (Number) The ID of the provider account associated with the virtual circuit.
- `status` (String) One of [planned, provisioning, active, offline, deprovisioning, decommissioned].
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags assigned to the object, by name.
- `tenant_id` (Number) The ID of the tenant associated with the virtual circuit.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) When the virtual circuit was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_updated` (String) When the virtual circuit was last changed.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) All tags assigned to the object, including those not managed by Terraform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the numeric NetBox ID of the object
terraform import netbox_virtual_circuit.example 1
```
